mechaber.he:
אם נאמן האדם לאסור יינו של חבירו. ובו ד' סעיפים:
האומר לחבירו נתנסך יינך אם הוא בידו נאמן ואפילו אם אינו עתה בידו שכבר הוחזר לבעלים אם בפעם ראשון שמצאו אמר לו נתנסך יינך נאמן אפי' אם הבעל מכחישו אבל אם אינו בידו ולא אמר כן לבעל בפעם ראשון שראהו וא"ל אחר כך אינו נאמן אם הבעל מכחישו (תוך כדי דבור) (מרדכי פרק האומר) או אומר איני יודע אבל אם שתק שתיקה כהודאה דמיא: הגה ומלמדי' אותו לכתחלה שיאמר איני מאמינך ואז לכ"ע שרי דבעלים נאמנים על שלהם (טור) ואם אין הבעלים מכחישין אותו אף על פי שמכחישו אחר לא מהני (הגהת מיימוני פי"א) מאחר שהבעלים שם ושותקין אבל אם אין הבעלים שם מהני (ארוך) ויש מי שכתב דעד אחד בהכחשה לאו כלום הוא (רשב"א סי' תקמ"ה) ואם הבעלים אומרים איני מאמינך אע"ג דבלבו מאמין לו כבי תרי אין להחמיר (ב"י בשם מרדכי) ודוקא ביין נסך שאין לדקדק בו כל כך אבל בשאר איסורים לא מהני אם אמר איני מאמינך אם מאמין בלבו: (ארוך כלל י"ג): והוא שיאמר לו נתנסך יינך בפניך או שאמר ליה ידעת דרגלים לדבר ואם שתק ואח"כ הכחישו ואמר מה ששתקתי תחילה לא בשביל שהודיתי אלא להתיישב ולחשוב בלבי לזכור אם הוא אמת נאמן: הגה ואם לא הגיד לו בפעם ראשון שמצאו ואומר לו אח"כ ואמר אמתלא למה לא אמר לו בראשונה יש לחוש לדבריו (הגהות מרדכי פ' האומר) וכל מי שנאמן על דבר ועדים מכחישין אותו אף על פי שיש לו מגו שהיה נאמן לאסרו בענין שלא היו העדים מכחישין אותו מ"מ מאחר שמכחיש העדים הוה ליה מגו במקום עדים ואינו נאמן אפילו בדבר איסור מ"מ לדידיה אסור משום דשוייה אנפשיה חתיכה דאיסורא. (כן משמע מב"י בשם תשובת הרשב"א) טבח שעשה סימן בבהמה כדרך שעושין בבהמות טריפות ואומר עליה שהיא טריפה וחוזר ואומר שכשירה היא ולא אמר כן תחלה רק שתשאר לו ליקח ממנה בשר יש מי שאומר מאחר שנותן אמתלא לדבריו נאמן ועיין לעיל סימן א' מדין עד אחד נאמן באיסורין ב' אחים אינם אלא כעד אחד לענין איסורים (תשובת הרשב"א סימן תקמ"ד) וכל הפסולי עדות כשרים לענין איסורים אם לא שחשוד לאותם דברים (ר"ן) אחד שאומר לשני שותפים נתנסך יינכם ואחד שותק והשני מכחישו לזה ששותק אסור ולשני ולכל העולם שרי. (הגהות אלפסי):
mechaber.en: If a person is trusted to forbid the wine of his fellow. In it are 4 seifim. One who says to his fellow, “Your wine was poured as a libation”: if it is in his hand, he is believed. And even if it is not in his hand now, for it was already returned to the owner — if the first time he found it he said to him, “Your wine was poured as a libation,” he is believed, even if the owner contradicts him. But if it is not in his hand, and he did not say so to the owner the first time he saw it, and afterwards he said to him — he is not believed if the owner contradicts him within “toch k’dei dibbur” (Mordechai, perek HaOmer), or he says, “I do not know.” But if he was silent, silence is like admission. {Rama: We teach him l'chatchila that he should say, “I do not believe you,” and then according to everyone it is permitted, for the owners are believed regarding what is theirs (Tur). And if the owners do not contradict him, even though another contradicts him, it does not help (Hagahot Maimoniot, chapter 11), since the owners are there and are silent; but if the owners are not there, it helps (Arukh). And some wrote that one witness in the face of contradiction is nothing (Rashba siman 545). And if the owners say, “I do not believe you,” even though in his heart he believes him as two witnesses, one should not be stringent (Beit Yosef in the name of Mordechai); and this is specifically regarding yayin nesech, for one need not be so exacting; but regarding other issurim it does not help if he said “I do not believe you” while he believes in his heart (Arukh, general rule 13).} And this is when he says to him “Your wine was poured as a libation” in your presence, or he said to him, “You know that there are indications for the matter.” But if he was silent and afterwards contradicted him and said, “What I was silent about at first was not because I admitted, but to settle and think in my heart, to remember whether it is true” — he is believed. {Rama: And if he did not tell him the first time he found it, and later says it and gives an excuse why he did not say it at first, one should be concerned for his words (Hagahot Mordechai, perek HaOmer). And anyone who is trusted regarding something and witnesses contradict him: even though he has a migo that he would have been believed to forbid it in a situation where witnesses were not contradicting him, nevertheless since he contradicts the witnesses it is a migo in the presence of witnesses, and he is not believed even regarding issur. Nevertheless, for himself it is forbidden because he has made it for himself a “chatichah d’issura” (so it appears from Beit Yosef in the name of a responsum of Rashba). A butcher who made a sign on an animal in the manner that is done on treifah animals, and says about it that it is treifah, and later says that it is kosher, and he did not say so initially except so that it would remain for him to take meat from it — there is one who says that since he gives an excuse for his words, he is believed; and see above siman 1 regarding the law that one witness is trusted regarding issurim. Two brothers are only like one witness regarding issurim (a responsum of Rashba siman 544). And all those disqualified for testimony are fit regarding issurim, unless he is suspected regarding those matters (Ran). One who says to two partners, “Your wine was poured as a libation,” and one is silent and the other contradicts: for the one who is silent it is forbidden, and for the other and for the whole world it is permitted (Hagahot Alfasi).}

siftei_kohen.he:
אם הוא בידו. ל' הטור כגון שנתנו בידו לשומרו ור"ל דל"ת דבידו היינו בידו לנסכו אלא דהיינו שנתנו בידו לשומרו והוי כבעליו עליו ולא מטעם מיגו וכ"פ הרא"ש פ' הנזקין בחילוק י"א והמרדכי ר"פ האשה רבה אבל הב"י לא הביא דברי הרא"ש ומרדכי אלו ואדרבה הביא בסתם דברי רש"י ור"ת והרשב"א שפירשו כל שבידו לטמא ואולי לזה השמיט כאן ל' הטור וכן בעט"ז פי' הטעם משום שישנו בידו לחסרו וכן הוכיח הרשב"א בחידושיו פרק הנזקין ריש דף ע"ט בראיות וכן משמע בתו' בקדושין פרק האומר (דף ס"ה ע"ב) דמהימן משום מגו ועפ"ז יש לדון במי שאומר לחבירו על יין מבושל שלו שנתנסך קודם הבישול אינו נאמן) אפי' הוא בידו כיון דלית ליה מגו:
נאמן. אפילו לא אמר ליה בפעם הראשון שמצאו:
אם בפעם כו' אפילו הבעל דין מכחישו. באמת זאת היא דעת התוספות והרא"ש ומרדכי ושאר הרבה פוסקים אבל קשה דהא כללא הוא לא יקום עד אחד באיש וגו' דעד א' אינו קם רק לשבועה ונהי דקי"ל עד א' נאמן באיסורים היינו היכא דאין הבע"ד מכחישו או במקום דאיכא מגו אבל במקום דליכא לא הא ולא הא לא מיסתבר כלל דעד א' יהא נאמן להכחיש הבע"ד ולהפסיד ממונו ואף בדאיכא מגו ק"ק דהא כתבו הרא"ש והט"ו בח"מ סימן ק"ח סי"ד דאינו נאמן (וכה"ג הקשו התוס' בעשרה יוחסין והרא"ש פ"ק דמציעא ושאר פוסקים אמ"ש רש"י דהיכא דאין מקחו בידו נאמן לומר לזה מכרתי אי נקט זוזי מחד דאמאי יהא נאמן טפי מעובד כוכבים דעלמא עכ"ד אע"ג דהיה בידו מתחלה) אלא דיש לחלק קצת ע"ש והשטה המחוורת בש"ס היא שטת הראב"ד והרשב"א דמפרשים הך דאמרינן בהנזקין דאי אשכחי' וא"ל מיד נאמן בשותק ומחלקין בין פועל דגרע מעד דעלמא ע"ש וכ"כ הר"ן בהנזקין והיא שטת האחרונים שהביא הר"ן פרק האומר וזהו דעת הרמב"ם סוף הלכות פסולי המוקדשין וסוף ה' מטמאי משכב ומושב דדוקא בשותק נאמן ע"ש ודו"ק:
נאמן. כתב הרב בתשוב' סי' ס"ו דאם הבעל מכחישו ואמר שלא א"ל בפעם הראשון ודאי הבעל נאמן ועיין עוד שם מדינים אלו:
אבל אם אינו בידו. פי' אפי' היה בידו מתחלה מ"מ כיון שאינו עתה בידו ולא א"ל בפעם הא' אינו נאמן אבל כשלא היה בידו מעולם אפי' א"ל בפעם הא' אינו נאמן כשהבע"ד מכחישו אלא בששותק כן מבואר בתוספות והרא"ש ומרדכי וסייעתו והמחבר קיצר בדבר:
אם הבעל מכחישו. ואז מותר לכל העולם וכן כתב הרב בסוף הסעיף ואפילו אמר איני יודע מותר לכל העולם כמ"ש כאו"ה כלל י"ג די"ג בשם ר"ח וכ"פ בד"מ:
או אומר כו'. כתוב במרדכי פ' האומר דאם א"ל שמא לא דקדקת חשיב כאלו מכחישו ומביאו בד"מ:
אינו יודע. ע"ל ס"ק ט"ו:
אבל אם שתק כו'. פי' אפי' אחר שלא היה בידו מעולם ולא א"ל בפעם הא' לעולם כיון דשתק כהודאה דמיא וז"ל הטור אבל אחר שאינו בידו או שלא אמ"ל השומר לבעליו בפעם הא' וא"ל אח"כ אינו נאמן ודוקא שהבעלים מכחישין אותו או אומר אינו יודע אבל אם שותק שתיקה כהודאה דמיא עכ"ל וכתב הב"ח ונראה לי מלשון הטור מדכתב אבל אחר שאינו בידו או שלא אמר השומר כו' ולא כתב או שלא אמר בפעם הא' אלמא משמע דבאחר שאינו שומר שלא היה בידו אין חילוק בין בפעם הא' לפעם הב' לעולם אם שותק כהודאה דמיא וכ"כ ב"י ע"ש הרשב"א בחידושיו כו' עכ"ל ותימא גדולה דהא גבי הכחשה הוא דכתב הטור או שלא אמר השומר כו' אבל בסיפא גבי שתיקה לא חילק ועוד שהרי עומד בשטת התוס' והרא"ש וסייעתם והם הקשו מהא דאביי דאמר עד אחד נאמן כששותק אע"ג שלא היה בידו מעולם אהך דהנזקין דאמר אביי גבי שומר דאם אינו בידו אינו נאמן ויישבו בדוחק ואם איתא הא אין התחלה לקושיא זו אלא אדרבה סברת התוס' והרא"ש היא להדיא הפוכה מסברת הרשב"א וס"ל דשומר עדיף מעד דעלמא כיון שהיה פעם אחד בידו והכי משמע נמי להדיא ממ"ש הרא"ש ואדרבה נמי קשה דאע"ג דמהימן ליה כו' ע"ש והכי מוכח נמי להדיא במרדכי פ' האומר גבי מ"ש שם וכתב ראבי"ה רבא נמי מודה באין בידו ושותק כדמשמע הכא כו' דגבי שומר שהיה בידו נמי אמרינן דשתיקה הוי הודאה אפי' בפעם ב' וע"ק דכיון דאמרינן שתיקה כהודאה דמיא מה חילוק בין שומר או עד דעלמא הא כל שא"ל בפניך נתנסך או ידעת רגלים לדבר ה"ל להשיבו ומדשתק הודה וא"כ אין חילוק וכך הקשה בד"מ על הרשב"א ומביאו הדרישה אלא דהד"מ לא הקשה כלום אהרשב"א דאיהו אזיל לטעמיה דס"ל בתשובה סימן שע"ו דהא דקאמר אביי שותק נאמן לאו משום דשתיקה כהודאה היא ואצ"ל בפניך וכה"ג אלא אפי' שותק מפני שאינו יודע בירור הדבר נאמן וכמ"ש בס"ק ט"ו בשמו ולכך מחלק בין שומר לאחר דשומר לא מהימן כולי האי דחזקת מיזהר זהיר כיון דעליה רמיא מילתא כו' אבל להטור דס"ל שתיקה כהודאה דמיא ודאי דאין חילוק אלא ודאי כך הוי פשט הטור אבל אחר שאינו בידו כלומר שלא היה בידו מעולם אפילו אמר ליה מיד אינו נאמן כל שהבעל מכחישו או אפי' שומר שהיה בידו אם לא א"ל בפעם הא' אינו נאמן כשמכחישו או אומר איני יודע אבל אם שותק אין חילוק בין אחר לשומר בין א"ל מיד או לא לעולם שתיקה כהודאה דמיא וכך הם דברי המחבר וכן מבואר בתוס' והרא"ש וסייעתם ונראה דהוי שותק בענין דודאי שתיקתו הודאה כגון דא"ל בפניך וכה"ג גם הרשב"א מודה דאין חילוק בין שומר לאחר בין א"ל מיד או לא לעולם נאמן וכל זה ברור:
שתיקה כהודאה דמיא. לאו כהודאה ממש דא"כ פשיטא וגם לא היינו צריכים לנאמנות העד ועוד דמוכח בפרק האומר (דף ס"ו ע"א) דאם היה העד גזלן אפילו שותק אינו נאמן אלא כיון ששותק נראה שיודע רגלים לדבר וסומך על העד כ"כ התוס' ר"פ האשה רבה וכ"כ התוס' פרק האומר שם ד"ה רבא והמרדכי לשם וצ"ע אהר"ן שדחק ליישב דברי התו' במ"ש דשתיקה כהודאה דמיא ונעלם ממנו דברי התוס' אלו ע"ש:
ומלמדין אותו כו'. פי' מלמדים אותו קודם שא"ל העד שכשיבא העד ויאמר לו יאמר לו מיד תוך כדי דיבור איני מאמינך ואין מלמדין אותו להכחישו דהיאך ילמדוהו לשקר:

If for the first time, etc., even if the owner of the wine contradicts him. In truth this is the view of Tosafot, the Rosh, Mordechai, and many other poskim; but it is difficult, for the principle is "one witness shall not rise against a man," and a single witness stands only for an oath; and although we hold one witness is believed in prohibitions, that is where the owner of the wine does not contradict him, or where there is a migu; but where there is neither this nor that, it is not reasonable at all that one witness should be believed to contradict the owner of the wine and cause him monetary loss; and even where there is a migu it is difficult, for the Rosh and Tur in Choshen Mishpat siman 108 seif 14 wrote that he is not believed (and similarly Tosafot challenged in Yuchasin, the Rosh in the first chapter of Bava Metzia, and other poskim, as Rashi explained: where the purchase is not in his hand he is believed to say "I sold to this one" if he took payment from one — why should he be more believed than an ordinary gentile? — end of his words, even though it was in his hand initially); but one may distinguish somewhat — see there; and the correct approach in the Gemara is the view of the Raavad and Rashba, who explain the case in Nezikin that if we find him and he says immediately he is believed in silence, and they distinguish between a worker, who is inferior to an ordinary witness — see there; and likewise the Ran in Nezikin; and it is the view of the Acharonim that the Ran brought in the chapter HaOmer; and this is the view of the Rambam at the end of Hilchot Pesulei HaMukdashin and at the end of Hilchot Metamei Mishkav uMoshav, that specifically in silence he is believed — see there, and examine carefully.

But if he was silent, etc. Meaning: even after it was never in his hand and he never told him the first time, since he was silent it is like admission; and such is the language of the Tur: but afterward, when it is not in his hand, or the guardian did not tell the owner the first time and afterward told him, he is not believed — and specifically when the owners contradict him or say they do not know; but if they are silent, silence is like admission — end of his words; and Bach wrote: it appears to me from the Tur's language, since he wrote "but afterward when it is not in his hand, or the guardian did not say," and did not write "or did not say the first time," it implies that afterward, when he is no longer the guardian and it was not in his hand, there is no distinction between the first time and the second time forever — if he is silent, silence is like admission; and likewise Beit Yosef there, Rashba in his chiddushim, etc. — end of his words; and one may raise a great astonishment, for regarding contradiction the Tur wrote "or the guardian did not say," but in the latter part regarding silence he did not distinguish; and further, behold he follows the view of Tosafot, the Rosh, and their supporters, and they challenged from that which Abaye said that a silent witness is believed even though it was never in his hand, against that which is in Nezikin regarding a guardian that if it is not in his hand he is not believed; and they resolved with difficulty; and if so, there is no beginning to this question — rather, on the contrary, the view of Tosafot and the Rosh is explicitly the opposite of Rashba's view, and they hold that a guardian is superior to an ordinary witness since it was once in his hand; and such appears explicitly from the Rosh's words; and on the contrary it is also difficult, for even though he is believed to him, etc. — see there; and such is proven explicitly in Mordechai in the chapter HaOmer regarding what is written there, and Rabbenu Yehuda wrote: Rava too agrees when it is not in his hand and he is silent, as appears here, etc., that regarding a guardian who was in his hand we also say silence is admission even the second time; and one may challenge: since we say silence is like admission, what difference between a guardian or an ordinary witness — for whoever was told "it was libated in your presence" or "you knew circumstantial evidence" should have answered him, and since he was silent he admitted; if so there is no distinction; and thus Darkei Moshe challenged Rashba, and he brings it Derishah; except Darkei Moshe did not challenge Rashba at all, for he follows his reasoning that that which Abaye says a silent witness is believed is not because silence is admission, and all the more "in your presence," and similarly; rather, even if he is silent because he does not know the matter clearly, he is believed, as written in s.k. 15 in his name; and therefore he distinguishes between a guardian and others, for a guardian is not so believed because he is presumed to be very careful since the matter rests upon him, etc.; but according to the Tur, who holds silence is like admission, certainly there is no distinction; but when it was never in his hand, even if he told him immediately, he is not believed as long as the owner contradicts him; or a guardian who was in his hand, if he did not tell him the first time, he is not believed when they contradict him or say they do not know; but if they are silent, there is no distinction between others and a guardian, whether he told him immediately or not forever — silence is like admission; and such are the words of the Mechaber, and so it is explained in Tosafot, the Rosh, and their supporters; and it appears this is silence in a matter where certainly his silence is admission, such as where he was told "in your presence," and similarly; Rashba too agrees there is no distinction between a guardian and others, whether he told him immediately or not — he is believed; and all this is clear.
Silence is like admission. Not literally like admission, for then it would be obvious, and we would not need the witness's credibility; and further, it is proven in the chapter HaOmer (daf 66 side 1) that if the witness was a robber, even if he is silent he is not believed; rather, since he is silent it appears he knows circumstantial evidence and relies on the witness — so wrote Tosafot in the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba, and likewise Tosafot in the chapter HaOmer there s.v. Rava, and Mordechai there; and it is difficult on the Ran, who forced himself to resolve the words of Tosafot with what is written that silence is like admission, and these words of Tosafot were hidden from him — see there.

Even though another contradicts him, it does not help. That which Darkei Moshe brought from the Gemara in the first chapter and was written thus in Shulchan Aruch — I did not find it in the hagahot before him; but Or Zarua general law 13 likewise wrote so in the name of Semag (and it is at the end of siman 223); but one may be astonished at this law, for Abaye who says in the Gemara "one witness told him and the other is silent — he is believed" learned it from what we taught in Keritot in the first chapter: they told him, he told one witness "you ate forbidden fat," and the other says "I did not eat" — he is exempt; the reason is that he said "behold he was silent" — he is believed; and at the beginning of that mishnah we taught: one witness says he ate and one witness says he did not eat — he brings a conditional guilt offering; and it must be when he is silent (due to admission, such as where they told him "you should have known," as written in the Sifrei — see there); for if they contradict him it is obvious; and all the more from the end that he is exempt — that even so the contradiction of the witness who says "he did not eat" to exempt him from a definite sacrifice proves that even though he was silent we do not say he admitted to this one who says "he ate"; nevertheless, since one witness contradicts him, one may say he relies on the contradictor, or he knows circumstantial evidence for this one and for that one; and even though where he is silent because he does not know the matter clearly he is not believed — that is different there, for the witness's testimony is not valid at all, for we require that the owner of the wine admit somewhat to him; or chelev is different, for there even if his heart tells him he brings a conditional guilt offering, as written in s.k. 13 in the name of the Yerushalmi — see there; nevertheless it is proven that even though the owners are there and silent, the contradiction of the witness helps; and it is strained to say that that which he says "it does not help" is only so the wine should be permitted with certainty, but it does not emerge from doubt; but it is not so, for it is in Semak siman 223 and Or Zarua there and Darkei Moshe in the name of the hagahot that the contradiction of the witness who says "it was not libated" does not help even to permit it to himself; and if it is a doubt, why should it not be permitted to the witness himself? And behold even regarding a married woman we hold that if one witness says her husband died and one witness says he did not die, if she married the one who says he died, even though each time he comes upon her he stands under a conditional guilt offering, she does not leave — as the Rambam wrote in chapter 12 of Hilchot Gerushin din 19, and as the Hagid proved there with clear proof from the Yerushalmi and other proofs as well; and even for the Ramban and Rosh in their responsum who disagree there — that is because since she is in the presumption of a married woman, we establish man against man and establish the woman in the presumption of a married woman, as is proven there; not so here; and one must say for Semak and Or Zarua that nevertheless there is an issur l'chatchila, and according to this view b'dieved one should not be stringent on the witness himself.
It helps. The law is difficult, for why does it help — behold even if they do not contradict him his testimony is nothing, since the owner of the wine is not before us, for it must be "in your presence" or "you knew," etc., as he concludes; and one may say his contradiction helps, for even if afterward he too says again before the owner of the wine and is silent he is not believed, since his silence is not full admission but that he knows circumstantial evidence and relies on the witness's words, as written in s.k. 9; therefore if he was already contradicted he no longer relies on him; and requires investigation for practical law.
And some wrote, etc. The rabbi's words here require great investigation, for it appears that for "some wrote" (and that is Rashba in responsum siman 345) even if the owners are not present, until this one who contradicts and says "it was not libated" — it is nothing; and likewise Pri Chadash explained, and Taz explained the reason: since Chazal said the witness who says "it was libated" is believed, it is like two witnesses, and the words of the one witness who says "it was not libated" are nothing against two — end of his words; and this is not so, for such is the language of Rashba there: "And what he said — one witness in prohibitions, in contradiction of the owner of the wine not in his presence — what is the law? Answer: one witness in contradiction is nothing, as is in Kiddushin at the end of the chapter HaOmer (daf 65 side 2) with two who came from overseas, etc.; and here even not in his presence, since the owner of the wine contradicts him, this one cannot forbid his own," etc. — end of his words; and he does not mean that one witness in contradiction is nothing — meaning the contradicting witness is nothing, for there at the end of the chapter HaOmer it is proven explicitly that the contradicted witness is nothing; and further, the questioner did not mention anything about the contradicting witness — for what purpose would Rashba precede to say the contradicting witness is nothing? And further, if so, what is the connection of "and here even not in his presence," etc., to the above? Rather the matter is clear that such is the thrust of his words: "One witness contradicting the owner of the wine is nothing, as is in the end of the chapter HaOmer," which challenges there "and is it reasonable — is one witness in contradiction believed?" — meaning where the owner of the wine contradicts him, for he does not stand except for an oath (and such appears explicitly in the Ran in chapter 2 of Ketubot s.v. terveyhu, and in the responsum of Maharik root 33, and in Terumat HaDeshen siman 212, and other poskim — such is their explanation, and I proved so in my chiddushim on Kiddushin, not like what is written in Rashi's explanation: "and is it reasonable — one witness in contradiction, where one witness contradicts him — is the contradicted witness believed?"; I later found in the responsum of Maharam Padua siman 32 that he wrote there are variant texts in Rashi's language on this — see there); "and here even not in his presence," etc., means: since we find that one witness contradicting the owner of the wine is nothing because one witness stands only for an oath — if so, here too even not in his presence, since the owner of the wine contradicts him, this one cannot forbid his own, for one witness stands only for an oath; but where the owner of the wine is not before us and one witness contradicts him — Rashba does not discuss this at all; and on the contrary it appears somewhat from there that he holds that whoever the witness contradicts and says "it was not impure," the witness who says "it was impure" is not believed — see there in what is written; and although there is an answer to his words — "one contradicting witness is nothing" — examine if we do not say there is a textual error in the responsum, as is somewhat proven there; and examine further; and another great astonishment: even if you say Rashba holds the contradicting witness is nothing, this is only according to his view that I brought in s.k. 15, that he holds even "in your presence," even when he does not know, he is believed; but according to what the rabbi ruled, that the witness who says "it was libated" is never believed except through the silence of the owner of the wine, which is like admission, and it must be "in your presence" or "you knew circumstantial evidence" — if so, when the owner of the wine is not before us, even without the contradicting witness, the witness who says "it was libated" is not believed at all; and this is clear, and so it is proven in Or Zarua general law 13 din 13 explicitly, where he wrote there: but if the owner of the wine was not there, etc., anyone can contradict him, etc., as is below — end of his words; and it must mean in what is written "as is below" in what is written there that it must specifically be "in your presence"; and requires investigation; and it is also astonishing according to Pri Chadash's explanation, that he explained the reason because the words of one are not in place of two — why should the witness who says "it was not libated" not also be counted as two? For since Chazal believed this one who says "it was libated," who removes from the presumption of permit — all the more they believed this one who says "it was not libated"; and everywhere we do not say the words of one are not in place of two except where he is believed like two and not the other, such as regarding one witness says died and one witness says did not die in chapter 2 of Ketubot — for they believed this one who says died like two, for a matter of prohibition is not less than two, and they believed the one who says died because of the stringency imposed upon her at the end, as is in the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba; and similarly in several places; not so here; therefore one must say that what the rabbi wrote "and some wrote that one witness in contradiction is nothing" refers to the beginning, even when the owners are present and silent — since one witness contradicts and says "it was not libated," this one who says "it was libated" is one witness in contradiction and is nothing; and it appears to the rabbi thus from Rashba's silence, and since he wrote "one witness in contradiction is nothing," it implies he rules generally that one witness is never believed except in general, but in contradiction always nothing, even if the owners are silent; and the language "one witness in contradiction" is thus precise — the contradicted witness is nothing; and likewise in the language of the Ran in chapter 2 of Ketubot s.v. terveyhu, etc.; and in the language of the Ramban that the Hagid brought in chapter 12 of Hilchot Gerushin din 19, and other poskim — this language too is found, "one witness in contradiction is nothing," and its explanation there is that the contradicted witness is nothing — see there; and this is why the rabbi elaborated and wrote "and some wrote that one witness in contradiction is nothing," and did not write briefly "and some disagree," or "some say" one witness, etc., or "some say" it only helps — rather he means: and some wrote simply that one witness in contradiction is nothing, and there is in his language that always it is nothing, even if the owner of the wine is silent; and so from what the Ran wrote in chapter 2 of Ketubot there regarding one witness says she was betrothed and one witness says she was not betrothed, and she is silent, and this is not a proper time, etc.; and further, since one witness in contradiction — why should she not marry? Behold one witness in contradiction is nothing — end of his words; it is proven that the contradicted witness is never nothing, even if the owner of the wine is silent; and examine; and one should not challenge that if so in Keritot, one witness says he ate and one witness says he did not eat, who brings a conditional guilt offering to exempt completely — one may say chelev is different, for even if his heart tells him he brings a conditional guilt offering; and such is in the Yerushalmi in the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba, halacha 4: two say she was betrothed and two say she was not betrothed — R. Yona compared it to chelev: these two say so-and-so ate forbidden fat and two say he did not eat — he brings a conditional guilt offering from doubt; and here she should be given a bill of divorce from doubt; R. Yosei said to him: do not compare it to chelev, for there even if he said "my heart tells me" he brings a conditional guilt offering — examine; conclusion from this: where one witness says "your wine was libated" and one witness contradicts him and the owner of the wine is there and silent — for Semak and Or Zarua the wine is forbidden from doubt, and also for the contradicting witness it is forbidden l'chatchila; and for the Ran, that one witness in contradiction is nothing, the wine is kosher; and so the view of Rashba appears somewhat; and where the owners are not present — according to the Tur and his supporters, who require that he say specifically "it was libated in your presence" or "you knew circumstantial evidence" — it is obvious that even without the witness who contradicts him he is not believed to say "it was libated," since the owner of the wine is not before us for silence to be like admission; and it is possible that here all permit, since one witness contradicts him; and nevertheless this law, whether for Semak and Or Zarua or for Rashba and the Ran, is permitted; and examine; and further there is here a great reasoning to permit, because one may say: establish man against man and establish the wine in its original presumption of permit; and such is the view of Tosafot in chapter 2 of Ketubot (daf 23 side 1) s.v. terveyhu: one witness says she was betrothed and one witness says she was not betrothed — she may marry even l'chatchila, because we establish man against man and establish the woman in the presumption of being unmarried; all the more here regarding stam yeinam; however all this is when the two witnesses came at once; but one after another, since the first witness's testimony was already accepted in court and judgment was rendered on the basis of his testimony (as is written below), it is like two witnesses; and when afterward one witness comes to contradict him, the words of one are not in place of two — so Tosafot in chapter 2 of Ketubot (daf 22 side 2 s.v. im ken) and in the chapter HaIsha Shalom (Yevamot daf 117), and likewise Nimukei Yosef in the chapter HaIsha Shalom; and such is proven explicitly in the Gemara there; except that Nimukei Yosef in the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba wrote in the name of the Ritva, who wrote in the name of his teacher z"l: specifically testimony of a matter of prohibition, for we require two, and they believed this one who says died like two; but in a general prohibition where one suffices, since they did not believe him except as one, when another comes and contradicts him it is contradiction of one against one — end of his words; and after him Maharshal followed in the first chapter of Chullin siman 9, and Bach at the end of siman 1; and they ruled not like Maharik root 33, who ruled regarding one who said about the slaughterer that he slaughtered improperly and the slaughterer contradicts that the slaughter was valid — because since they believed the slaughterer it is like two, and the words of one are not in place of two; but the Mechaber at the end of siman 1 ruled like Maharik; and so it appears explicitly from the words of the Rosh in the chapter Nezikin and Mordechai in the chapter HaIsha Rabba in the explanation of fourteen distinctions in distinction 5; and likewise it appears in Tosafot in Keritot at the beginning of the chapter Amru Lo; and such is the view of the Rama that the Tur brought in Choshen Mishpat at the end of siman 66, that even in a matter that is not a matter of prohibition we say thus; and it appears to me there is proof for their words from the end of Sotah regarding one witness says I saw the killer and one says I did not see — we say there too: wherever the Torah believed one witness, behold he is like two, etc.; and it is possible to say that the view of the Ritva and his supporters is that certainly where Scripture revealed to us that one witness is believed, he is like two, for the Torah believed him like two; but where Scripture did not reveal to us except that it is reasonable or it is a rabbinic enactment that he is believed — such as a piece, doubt fat doubt milk, and one witness says it is fat; or where one witness told him "your wine was libated" and he is silent, and similarly; and everywhere we say one witness is believed in prohibitions — since Scripture did not reveal it to us, he is not considered like two; except that for woman's testimony, where by law two are required and Chazal believed one like two, the words of one are not in place of two; and there regarding the heifer whose neck is broken we derive from Scripture "it is not known" that one witness is believed, as is there; and according to this one may say the Rama agrees with the Ritva, that he speaks there regarding an oath, for Scripture revealed to us that he stands for an oath; however Maharik and his supporters do not disagree on this, that at once we do not say it is like two; and even though in the case of the slaughterer it is at once — it is different there, since they believed the slaughterer because of the presumption that most experts are found at slaughter — they assist him, as is in Maharik there; if so it is as if his testimony was already accepted in court — you will know, for otherwise it would be difficult on the rabbi, who wrote here divided opinions and at the end of siman 1 ruled like the Mechaber and Maharik; and examine; and this is also the reason that wherever one witness is believed from the Torah, even if one contradicts him immediately at once, his words are nothing, as Tosafot wrote in chapter 2 of Ketubot and in the chapter HaIsha Shalom there — because since the Torah believed one witness, it is as if his testimony was already accepted in court; and with this it appears clear to resolve what Tosafot wondered in the chapter Mi Shekinei from that which appears there in the Gemara regarding another witness who says she was defiled, that it is like two and the words of the one who says she was not defiled are nothing in place of two — from where do we say in HaIsha Shalom regarding one witness says died, specifically they permitted her on the basis of the court; and they entered with great difficulty, and even so Rashi and as appears from their words there did not resolve — see there; and according to what I wrote it is satisfactory, for that case in HaIsha Shalom is different, for the one witness who says died is not believed except rabbinically, specifically when he says before the court, for we hold a woman married on one witness not through the court must leave; and therefore as long as the court did not permit her, his testimony is not considered like two; but regarding sotah, the Merciful One believed one witness, as we derive from "if there was not in her," etc.; if so, immediately when he testified it is like two; such appears clear to me; and examine these laws well.
Even though in his heart he believes him like two, etc. It appears he means: even though his heart tells him and it is clear to him that the witness, if he did not know the matter clearly, would not have said it was libated, and he believes him in his heart like two witnesses — nevertheless, since he expresses with his lips "I do not believe you," one should not be stringent; and such appears in Pri Chadash; and in truth it appears at first glance in Mordechai that he understood Rabbenu Tam's words thus — see there; but in truth it appears to me that this did not enter Rabbenu Tam's mind, for if he believes him in his heart like two, how does he fulfill his obligation to Heaven and say with his mouth "I do not believe you"? For if he believes him in his heart like two, and it is like two saying "your wine was libated," how can he say "I do not believe you" like two? Rather Rabbenu Tam means: even if he believes him like two, he can say "I do not believe you" — meaning, for this matter you are not believed to me like two; and if the owner of the wine said so, we certainly say he speaks truth, for in his heart he does not believe him like two; and we should not say that since until now he believed him like two, the owner of the wine can no longer say "I do not believe you," for it is as if two witnesses came and told him "your wine was libated"; rather, since he said "I do not believe you," he nullified his credibility; and in Mordechai too one may explain thus — see there, and examine; even though it is somewhat forced in the language, it is preferable to me thus, so we do not say Rabbenu Tam holds that even though he believes him in his heart like two, he may come to say "I do not believe you"; and no author is found who wrote so in the name of Rabbenu Tam or who thinks so; and even if we say Rabbenu Tam holds thus — nevertheless R. Meir and Rabbenu Yehuda disagree, and Mordechai brought them in his conclusion; and such appears the view of Tosafot in Kiddushin (daf 65 side 2) s.v. nitmeu, and likewise in Hagahat Mordechai in the chapter HaMafkid in the name of R. Yaakov of Kinin; and even though Semak siman 253 and likewise Or Zarua at the end of general law 13 ruled like Rabbenu Tam — that is because they understood Rabbenu Tam's view as I wrote, for the language "believes him in his heart" is not found there; and examine; Bach too ruled stringently, even regarding stam yeinam, if he believes him in his heart — see there.
Provided he says to him "it was libated in your presence," or told him "you knew," etc. For otherwise it is not silence like admission, for that which he is silent because he does not know the matter clearly — that is the view of Tosafot, the Rosh, Mordechai, and Beit Yosef brings them; but one may be astonished, for behold the view of Rashba in responsum siman 376, and the Ran in the chapter HaOmer, and the Ritva, and Nimukei Yosef in the first chapter of HaIsha — that even if he did not tell him "in your presence" or "you knew," etc., but even if he is silent because he does not know the matter clearly, he is believed (and Beit Yosef did not bring them); and likewise the view of Raavan siman 64; and likewise it appears the view of the Raavad that Rashba brought in his chiddushim in the chapter Nezikin at the beginning of daf 39 — see there; and also R. Yerucham at the end of netiv 15, and the Rivash siman 245, wrote that there are disputants on Tosafot in this; and it is the view of the Acharonim that the Ran brought in the chapter HaOmer; and likewise Tosafot Rid agreed in Kiddushin daf 65 side 2 — see there; and it appears to me that this is the view of the Rambam, who wrote in chapter 9 of Hilchot Nezirut: if he was silent or was in doubt, he brings a sacrifice even on one witness; and in the Sifrei I wrote that such appears to me the main point from the Gemara in the chapter HaOmer (daf 66 side 1) from the blind man and Mina the king; and further from the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba, that the Gemara needs to say that one witness is believed in prohibitions even to remove a forbidden matter from its presumption of permit without silence like admission — it needs a source there; and it asks from where do we know; and it needs to derive from tevel and similar; and certainly there it is different because it is in his hand; and if so, although it was not resolved — nevertheless from where do we know for the other side that he is not believed? And if so, although for permit we hold stringently — nevertheless for issur perhaps he is believed, for certainly if he is believed to permit, all the more he is believed for issur; as the Rosh wrote in the chapter Nezikin, and Mordechai in the chapter HaIsha Rabba in fourteen distinctions — "all the more" is for issur than for permit; and further proof from the first chapter of Gittin (daf 2 side 2) and the first chapter of HaIsha Rabba, that it says there: say that we say one witness is believed in prohibitions — such as a piece, doubt milk doubt fat, that forbidden matter was not established; but here forbidden matter was established, for a woman is prohibited, not less than two — examine; and from that it mentions "it is a matter of prohibition," etc., and did not mention briefly "but here forbidden matter was established — no"; and further — examine; one must say as Tosafot wrote there in the name of R. Yitzchak, and Rashba in his chiddushim there, that in HaIsha Rabba regarding other prohibitions we are in doubt whether he is believed even when forbidden matter was established and not in his hand; and it says it is a matter of prohibition — that even for permit it remains in doubt, all the more for issur; and further, that below siman 141 Beit Yosef brought on daf 243 at the end of side 3 Rashbatz on a mikveh that was filled and we do not know if it was filled properly or not — that if we know who filled it, we ask his mouth, for one witness is believed in prohibitions even where forbidden matter was established, and even where it is not in his hand to fix, as is in Chullin and Gittin and several places — end of his words; behold he holds he is believed to permit, and all the more to forbid; and even though the rabbi there at the end of seif 4 wrote he is not believed except where it is in his hand to fix it, and that is from the words of Maharik root 15 — one may say that is because we are in doubt and go stringently; and if so, here he is believed from doubt stringently; and further it appears to me proof from what we say in Keritot in the first chapter Amru Lo: it teaches — they told him, "you ate forbidden fat," he brings a sin offering; they said, "how many were there?" — two; and what did he tell them? If we say he was silent and did not contradict them, but on silence of two he brings a sin offering — on silence of one I do not say the intermediate position: one witness says he ate and he says "I did not eat" — he is exempt; the reason is he contradicts him; but silence obligates, etc.; and if so, why does it challenge? And it answers there in a strained version: say the beginning that he is exempt is when they did not tell him "you should have known"; and further, why does it challenge from the intermediate position — let it challenge from the beginning: one witness says he ate and one witness says he did not eat — he brings a conditional guilt offering; the reason is one witness says he did not eat — otherwise he would be liable; it must deal with silence, for if he contradicts it is obvious he is exempt; and what Tosafot wrote there — likewise it could challenge from the beginning — is not so clear that this is a passage to challenge the beginning against the intermediate and not challenge from the beginning itself; rather certainly from the beginning it asks: one may say that that which he was silent he is liable is when they told him "you should have known," as Tosafot wrote in the chapter HaOmer; but from the intermediate position it deduces the reason that he said "he did not" — he contradicts explicitly; behold he was silent — no; even if it is not because of admission, nevertheless since he does not contradict him, he is believed — see there, and examine; however the view of Semak siman 223 and 205, and Hagahat Maimoni chapter 1 law 41, and R. Yerucham at the end of netiv 15, and in Agudah, and Or Zarua at the end of general law 23 — like the Tur; however certainly in practice Rashba and his supporters agree that if it is not in his hand and he did not tell him the first time he found it, he is not believed if the owner of the wine is not silent due to admission, as is proven in Nezikin; and they wrote the reason regarding a worker: since he accepted to do it properly, he is presumed to be very careful, and therefore he is not believed; and see in s.k. 3 and s.k. 8.
[And brother] denied. I do not know what I have done before, but if I have said to me, I do not know what I have been paralyzed, not because I have been faithful to the Almighty, and it is proven to be the case of the X-Men
What I was silent, etc., but to settle, etc. Rabbeinu Yerucham likewise wrote so at the end of netiv 15; however in the second part of Netiv 15 he wrote that if he told him "it was libated in your presence" and he is silent, and afterward he returned and said "I was not silent except because I did not care about the witness's words" — it does not help, since one witness is believed in prohibitions; but in a matter of prohibition where not less than two are required, if he said "I was silent because I did not care about the witness's words" — it helps; examine — his words are additional explanation.
“There is someone who says ‘faithful’. At the end of C. C.C., the author wrote only that he was faithful and only so many of his sons, and here he wrote in his tongue that he had written, because he had written in his book, and that he had to do so, and that he had to do so with him, and that he would not be a part of him
And all those invalid for testimony, etc. This law is written in Darkei Moshe in the name of the Ran, and likewise it was written in Shulchan Aruch; and requires investigation, for the Ran in Kiddushin in the chapter HaOmer wrote explicitly that those invalid for testimony are not believed in prohibitions; and in responsum siman 25 he ruled that even one who is suspect regarding that matter is fit to testify regarding others — such as to say this meat was slaughtered properly, and similarly; and it appears one should distinguish: to permit, certainly he is believed to testify, for we hold one who is suspect regarding a matter testifies for him, as above siman 119 s.k. 18; but in the chapter HaOmer he deals explicitly with coming to forbid another's — such as to say "your wine was libated" — then he is not believed except through the silence of the owner of the wine, who relies on the words of the fit witness, as the Ran wrote there; and therefore, whoever is invalid does not rely on him, and it is not enough in his regard to forbid another's; nevertheless for the rabbi it is difficult, for behold he speaks now regarding "your wine was libated," and according to the Ran those invalid for testimony are not believed; and even if you say he deals with testifying to permit — it is difficult, for in such a case the Ran holds that even one who is suspect is believed, and such we hold above siman 119 seif 7 and siman 124 seif 9; and requires investigation; I returned and examined Darkei Moshe, and such is its language: Rashba wrote in responsum siman 264 that two brothers are only like one witness for prohibitions, whether to uphold a matter or regarding contradiction; further the Ran wrote siman 350 that even one unfit for monetary testimony is believed to testify in prohibitions if he is not suspect regarding that matter — end of his words; and it appears this "further the Ran wrote" is a textual error, for if so it is not relevant to say siman 350; and further, if so it should have said "the Ran wrote," what is "further wrote"? Rather one must say: further Rashba wrote, for Rashba wrote so in responsum siman 350: all those invalid for testimony are fit in prohibitions, and even an apostate for one matter is fit for another matter that is not that matter — until here is his language — see there; and not as written in Shulchan Aruch "Ran" (and in Rashba too it appears there he deals with testifying to permit; but when testifying to forbid it appears he agrees with the Ran that those invalid for testimony are not believed, as appears in the Gemara in the chapter HaOmer (daf 66 side 1), and as written in s.k. 9 in the name of Tosafot and Mordechai, and likewise in the responsum of Rashba at the end of siman 376); and nevertheless requires investigation, for it appears Rashba in responsum siman 350 deals specifically with an apostate — meaning one who is a habitual offender; but regarding one who is suspect, behold he wrote in responsum siman 64 that even one suspect regarding that matter is believed to testify regarding others; and likewise above siman 2 s.k. 20 in the name of Turat Chaim and Kessef Mishneh, to distinguish between apostate and suspect — see there; and one may resolve that the rabbi too, when he says "unless he is suspect regarding that matter," speaks of an apostate regarding that matter; and in siman 119 seif 7 he deals with suspect and not apostate; and even though there he says "one who is well known for a transgression" — meaning he is well known to have done the transgression once, which makes him suspect and not a habitual offender to be an apostate; however in siman 124 seif 9 regarding coerced persons, they are certainly habitual offenders; and it is possible that since they do so out of coercion and pressure, we judge them as suspect; and examine. And regarding the testimony of gentiles — poskim wrote in several places that gentiles are not believed, neither for issur nor for heter; and see above siman 118 s.k. 37, and siman 122 s.k. 3, and at the end of siman 129, and siman 130 at the end of seif 8 in the hagahah; and it appears that even if he has no benefit in his testimony, he is not believed to testify regarding others; and even though Semag negative commandment 137 on daf 41 at the end of side 2 wrote in the name of Rav Hai Gaon that we do not rely on the words of a gentile, neither for issur nor for heter — for issur, from what we say in the last chapter of Yevamot: a gentile who was selling produce in the market and said "these fruits are orlah," "these are tithed" — he said nothing; he did not intend this except to improve his sale, etc. — end of his words; it is not to say that specifically where he has benefit in his testimony, such as there where he intends to improve his sale, but generally he is believed to forbid; for the principle is always applied that we never rely on gentiles; rather the reason that he did not intend except to improve his sale is not precise, but the same applies everywhere one can find some excuse; and such appears in the responsum of Maharil siman 38; and likewise it appears in the Gemara in the last chapter of Yevamot; or also specifically there this reason is needed, since the produce is his; and likewise it appears in Turat Chaim general law 32 din 9; I later found likewise in the responsum of Rashba siman 118 explicitly — see there; and now one may ask on the proof from that passage in Yevamot, for they are the words of Rashbag and Rabbi — behold the Tosafeta disagrees, that a gentile is believed to be stringent and not to be lenient, and we hold the halacha is like Rabbi over his colleague (however in Mordechai in the chapter Elu Megalchin, and in Hagahat Maimoni chapter 6 of Hilchot Avodah Zarah, they brought the Tosafeta — the words of Rabbi: Rashbag says a gentile is believed to be stringent, etc.; however it is explained there in their words that we hold like Rashbag, that a gentile is believed, etc. — see there; and see above siman 16 s.k. 23); rather certainly, as the Rosh wrote in the chapter Elu Megalchin in the name of Maharam: Rabbi only disagrees because the produce is his; but generally he agrees with Rashbag; and such is proven there in the Rosh, that for Rashbag he holds that generally he is not believed, even without the reason that he did not intend except to improve his sale — not like the view of Maharshal that I brought above siman 122 in s.k. 4; and take this principle in your hand, that we always dismiss the testimony of a gentile as though he does not exist, and his words do not raise or lower regarding others; and such we say below siman 139 s.k. 63; however where he speaks innocently, his law was already explained in siman 98 s.k. 2 and siman 313 s.k. 4.

אבל בשאר איסורים לא מהני כו'. כי יש חולקין וס"ל דכל שהוא מאמין בלבו שאומר אמת אין מועיל מה שמכחישו ועל זה נאמר ויראת מאלהיך:
אלא להתיישב ולחשוב בלבי כו'. משמע לי באם לא אמר כך אלא אמר שתקתי שהייתי סבור כיון שאני איני יודע ואתה יודע בבירור ועכשיו שמעתי מאחרים שאינך נאמן ומברר זה מאותן אחרים שהגידו לו כן דנאמן הוא בכך וכאלו אמר מתחלה איני יודע וראייה לזה מח"מ סימן כ' שהביא רמ"א שאם הביא ראיה שלא ידע תחילה מאלו עדים כו' וה"נ דכוותיה אבל אם אמר תחלה שתקתי שלא חשתי להשיבך אינו נאמן אע"פ שבח"מ סי' פ"א מצינו שיכול לומר כן לענין הודאות ממון שאני התם דיכול לומר אני ידעתי האמת שלא יזיק לי דבריך שאתה אומר שיש לך מנה בידי כיון שאין אני מוציא מפי שום דבר אבל כאן אין אדם עשוי שלא לחוש אם אומרים שהוא שותה איסור וע"פ דרך זה נ"ל ליישב מה שכתב ב"י בשם הרשב"א הא דמחלקינן כאן בין פעם הא' או לא דוקא בפועל או שומר אבל עד דעלמא נאמן אפילו לא אמר ליה בפעם הראשון שמצאו שמא לא נזכר בפעם הראשון דלאו עליה רמיא או שלא רצה להעיד לו ולבתר כן נמלך ואמר ליה עכ"ל. והקשה עליו בד"מ דע"כ הא דעד דעלמא נאמן היינו כשבעלים שותקין ואם כן פשיטא שאין לחלק בין פעם הראשון לפעם השני דמ"מ שתיקתו כהודאה בשלמא בשומר יש לחלק שפיר דפעם הראשון הוי שומר שלא במקצת ולא בפעם השני אבל במקום שהאיסור משום שתיקת הבעלים מה לי פעם הראשון ומה לי פעם שני עכ"ל ולי נראה דלא קשה מידי דהוי אמינא שיכול הבעל לומר כיון שכבר ראית אותי ולא אמרת לי דבר לאפרושי מאיסורא ועכשיו אתה אומר לי אין זה אלא דרך שחוק והיתול ועל כן לא חששתי להשיבך קמ"ל דלא אמרינן כן אלא נאמן אף בזה כיון שהוא אינו שומר שלו ובאמת רבותא גדולה היא:
טבח שעשה סי' בו'. בסי' א' סעיף י"ג כתבתי שאין לפסוק כן וכאן מצאתי בד"מ שגם הוא הקשה כן וכתב בסוף ואולי יש לחלק וצ"ע עכ"ל:

But the other prohibitions are not from me. For there is a sin that Hashem believes in his heart that says the truth is not beneficial for what is revealed and that is said and seen from your Hashem:
But to settle and think in my heart. It means to me that I am not saying so, but I say that I am not sure and you know clearly, and now I have heard from others that you are not faithful and that of those who have given him that he is faithful to him, and that he has said, “I do not know that I am not afraid of him, but that I am not faithful to him.” I knew the truth that you were saying you had a dose in my hands that I was not doing anything but here there was no man who would not feel if he was drinking a ban and that way was to settle what he wrote in the name of the Bible, but here there is no man who is not afraid to feel whether he is drinking a ban or not even for the first time, but that he did not even say to me that he did not remember the first time He was in the house and said to me. נאמן. כתב הש"ך ואפילו לא אמר לו בפעם הראשון שמצאו והטעם דנאמן משום מגו דבידו לנסכו וע"פ זה יש לדון במי שאומר לחבירו על (*) [אבל ז"א דע"כ מיירי כאן בגוונא דלא מקרי הפ"מ דאם לא כן למה צריך ס' נגד הקילוח]. יין מבושל שלו שנתנסך קודם הבשול אינו נאמן אפילו הוא בידו כיון דלית ליה מגו עד כאן לשונו:
מכחישו. והש"ך חולק על זה וס"ל דדוקא אם הבעלים שותקים הוא נאמן אבל אם הבעלים מכחישים אותו אינו נאמן כדאי' בח"מ סי' ק"ח סי"ד וכ' הר"ב בתשובה סי' ס"ו דאם הבעל מכחישו בזה שלא א"ל בפעם הראשון שמצאו ודאי הבעל נאמן ע"ש:
אינו. ואז מותר לכל העולם דאפילו אמר איני יודע מותר לכל העולם כ"כ בד"מ וכ' המרדכי דאם א"ל שמא לא דקדקת חשוב כאילו הכחישו:
כהודאה. פי' אפילו אמר שלא היה בידו מעולם ולא א"ל בפעם הא' לעולם כיון דשתיקה כהודאה דמיא ואין חילוק בין פועל לשומר בין א"ל מיד או לא הוי שתיקה כהודאה ולאו כהודאה ממש אלא כיון ששותק נראה שיודע רגלים לדבר וסומך על העד כ"כ התוס' עכ"ל הש"ך:
ומלמדים. פי' מלמדים אותו קודם שא"ל העד שכשיבא העד ויאמר לו יאמר לו מיד תוך כדי דיבור איני מאמינך ואין מלמדים אותו להכחישו דהיאך ילמדוהו לשקר (ובנה"כ פי' דמלמדין אותו לומר איני יודע ע"ש):

מהני. כתב הש"ך הל' קשה דמאי מהני הא אפילו לא יכחיש אין עדותו כלום כיון דאין הבע"ד לפנינו דהא צ"ל בפניך או ידעת כו' וי"ל דמהני הכחשתו דאפי' אומר אחר כך גם כן בפני הבע"ד ושותק אינו נאמן דכיון דטעמא דשתיקה וכו' דסומך על דברי העד כמ"ש לעיל הילכך אי איתכחיש כבר תו לא סמיך עליה וצ"ע לדינא עד כאן לשונו (ובנה"כ מתרץ דהא דכתב המחבר דצריך לומר בפניך וכו' מיירי דוקא כשהבעלים בכאן רק לענין שתיקה כהודאה בזה קאמר דצ"ל בפניך משא"כ אם הבעלים מתו או הלכו למה"י ועד א' אומר שיין זה נתנסך ולית מאן דמכחיש ליה פשיטא דנאמן לזה כתב דאם אחר מכחישו האחר נאמן ע"ש):

ויש מי כו'. כמש"ש בקדושין ע"א בהכחשה כו' וער"ן בפ"ב דכתובות גבי ע"א אומר נתקדשה כו' ועח"מ סי' פ"ב סי"ב וסי' מ"ו סל"ז ועבה"ג שם ס"ק כ' בשם הריטב"א. וסברא הראשוגה ס"ל מאחר שהבעלים שם ושותקין הוי כהודאה ועש"ך:
והוא שיאמר כו'. תוס' שם וש"פ וראיה מב"מ ל"ז ב' וע' במרדכי דקדושין שם:
ואם שתק כו'. ג"כ מגמ' דב"מ הנ"ל. שם ושם. וכ"ז שיטת התוס' ורא"ש ומרדכי וש"פ הנמשכין אחריהם אבל הרמב"ן והרשב"א והריטב"א בקדושין שם הקשו על שיטתם חדא דלא הל"ל בקדושין שם ע"א כו' נאמן דהא לאו משום נאמנותו אלא משום שהבעלים שותקים והל"ל א"ל ע"א אכלת חלב חייב נטמאו טהרותיך כו' טמאות כלישנא דמתני' וכמ"ש ביבמות שם ממאי דנאמן דלמא כו' ועוד דכולה שמעתא דקדושין איפכא משמע דהא אשתו זינתה דפליג רבא ואמר הוי דבר כו' ואי משום הודאתו ל"ל שנים הא שויה עלי' חתיכה דאיסורא והא רבא מודה בהנך לאביי ועוד ההוא סמיא לא ידע אי קושטא קאמר ופירשה אביי אי מהימן לך דלאו גזלנא כו' ועובדא דינאי הא צווח וקטיל. אלא דכל אדם נאמן לעולם אפי' לא היה בידו מעולם בשותק אפילו לא היה לו לידע או שאומר איני יודע ובכה"ג ההיא דקדושין וההיא דגטין איירי בפועל דעליה רמיא לאודועיה ולכן אינו נאמן אלא דוקא בידו או בפעם ראשון אבל במכחישו לעולם אינו נאמן בכ"ע וכ"כ הר"ן בגטין שם בקיצור וכ' הרשב"א וא"ת מנ"ל לאביי דקאמר ותנא תונא כו' דלמא משום דשתיקה כהודאה כמ"ש ביבמות שם י"ל דה"ק טעמא כו' דוקא לא הא אמר א"י (מהימן) דאל"כ ליתני א"י ומ"ש ביבמות שם וממאי דמשום דמהימן כו' קאי אמש"ש מדאורייתא מנ"ל כו' ואכתי מדאורייתא מנ"ל ומש"ש תדע דקתני כו' סוגיא דשם כההוא סברא שאמרו בכריתות י"ב א' טעמא דרבנן משום דאדם נאמן כו' אבל אביי סבר דטעמא משום מיגו מתרצינן לדיבוריה ולההוא לישנא רישא משום דנאמן הוא דכי קפטרי רבנן משום דלא מהימני במכחישין משום מיגו א"נ כההיא לישנא דמוקים שם מתני' כר"מ. והא דקאמר וצריכא כו' ה"ק דסד"א דטעמא לאו משום נאמנות אלא משום דשתיקה כהודאה דמיא ע"ש שהאריך והר"ן הביאו אבל כ' דשיטת תוס' עיקר כי כן מוכיחין סוגיות הנ"ל אלא דטעם שתיקה כהודאה הוא משום העדאת העד דגזירת הכתוב הוא דכל דשתיק העד נאמן ולכן כל שאין העד נאמן דהיינו גזלן וכיוצא אינו נאמן. ובזה מתורץ מה שהקשה דלמה קאמר נאמן וכן מה שהקשה ממש"ש דלאו גזלנא כו' וז"ש רבא אין דבר שבערוה כו' ר"ל בערוה ע"א אין נאמן כלל והוי כגזלן או פסול ומ"ש ביבמות שם וממאי משום כו' ה"ק ממאי דנאמן אפילו באומר אני יודע דלמא אינו יודע כמכחישו אלא דוקא היכא דאשתיק ועובדא דינאי דלמא פ"א שתק וכנ"ל דודאי תוך כ"ד ע"ש:
ואם לא כו'. כמ"ש בכתובות כ"ב א' ועבא"ע סי' קנ"ב ס"ו:
וכל מי שנאמן כו'. כמ"ש מנו במקום עדים לא אמרינן בפ"ו דב"מ (פ"א ב') ופ"ג דב"ב וש"מ:
מ"מ לדידיה כו'. כמ"ש בכתובות כ"ג ב' ועתוס' דיבמות מ"ז א' ד"ה נאמן כו' וד"ה ואין כו':
טבח כו'. עמ"ש בס"ס א':
וכל הפסולי כו'. אבל הר"ן כתב דאינן נאמנין דלה"ק אי מהימן לך דלאו גזלנא הוא כו' כנ"ל וצ"ע וכן מ"ש אם לא שחשוד כו' הא אמרינן לעיל סי' קי"ט ס"ז ובשל אחרים כו' דקי"ל בפ"ח דיומא ובבכורות ל"ה ב' כרשב"ג דאמר נאמן על של חבירו כו' אלא דלהתיר נאמן אף החשוד אבל לאסור דנאמן מכח עדותו כל הפסולין אינן נאמנין כנ"ל וכן הקשה בש"ך וצ"ע:
(ליקוט) וכל הפסולי עדות כו'. דקי"ל החשוד לדבר אחד אינו חשוד כו' [ועתוס' דבכורות ל"ו א' ד"ה אימור כו'] כמ"ש בסי' קי"ט ס"ד וס"ז:
אם לא כו'. ע"ש ס"ז דלא כ"כ שכ' ובשל אחרים כו' אבל כדברי הרב כן עיקר כמש"ש (בס"ק י"ח) (ע"כ):
beur_hagra.en:
If it is, etc. Abaye's words — Rava does not explain them, and these acts of designation. And Rashi explained that he has in his power to defile it and ruin it, and he is believed because of migo. And Rosh there and Mordechai chapter HaIsha Rabba wrote because he is like the owner; and proof from what he wrote regarding the mentions in it, etc., even though they were already written and it is not in his hand; and likewise in purities too there is no need for migo, for he is obligated to pay; and in Yevamot there — except that afterward, etc., because it is in his power to fix it — are we dealing with fools that he would separate terumah on his fellow's produce? And see Mordechai there:
And even if, etc. For we establish the halachah follows Rava; and even though those acts there are like Abaye — the Rosh already answered there — see there:
Even as a. He had never been faithful in his hand as "the Holy One" and he was given the name of his son-in-law, and he was given the word of his son and his father's son, and he was given his name to him, "And he was given his name to him."
But if they are . If he was in his hand, he was not faithful
Within the time of speech. For otherwise behold he already admitted; and in the first chapter of Bava Metzia 6a and in Bava Batra 138a:
Or says, etc. From what he wrote: and he told him in Zevachim, etc., and there he cannot contradict him — Mordechai in Kiddushin there:
But if you are silent.” He had never been in his hand like a saint there:
And we teach him, etc. Tur; and see above in the gloss "and if the owners," etc., "even though in his heart," etc.; and see there in Hagahot Maimoniyot, who challenged: if so, Shmuel should have told the blind man "say I do not believe you"; and likewise Tosafot in Kiddushin there — if he is believed like two, even if they contradict him he is believed — reject that proof; and see Shach s.k. 15:
And then according to all, etc. It is the matter in its own right, like "your ox was sodomized" — permitted for the Most High, and the like:
And some, etc. As he wrote in Kiddushin 71a regarding contradiction, etc.; and in Ran chapter 2 of Ketubot regarding one witness who says "she was betrothed," etc.; and in Orach Mishpat siman 82 seif 2 and siman 46 s.l. 37; and in Bach there s.k. 20 in the name of Ritva. And the first reasoning holds: since the owners are there and are silent, it is like admission — and see Shach:
He said yes. Hashem’s name is “Ps 119:105; 119:105; 119:130].”
And if he was silent, etc. Also from the Gemara in Bava Metzia cited. There. And there. And all this is the view of Tosafot, Rosh, Mordechai, and Shitat HaKadmonim who follow them; but Ramban, Rashba, and Ritva in Kiddushin there challenged their view: one, that it should not have said in Kiddushin there 71a, etc., "he is believed," for it is not because of his credibility but because the owners are silent — it should have said "he told him one witness: you ate forbidden fat, your purities became impure," etc., "impure" in the language of the mishnah; and as written in Yevamot there — whence is he believed? Perhaps, etc.; and further, the entire discussion in Kiddushin implies the opposite, for "his wife committed adultery" — Rava disagrees and says it becomes a matter, etc.; and if because of his admission, why need two? Behold he made upon her a piece of prohibition; and Rava agrees with those to Abaye; and further, that blind man did not know if he spoke truth, and Abaye explained: if you believe me that I am not a robber, etc.; and the case of King Yannai — he shouted and killed. Rather every person is always believed even if it was never in his hand, when silent — even if he had no way to know, or says "I do not know"; and in such a case that in Kiddushin and that in Gittin deals with a worker upon whom it is incumbent to inform, and therefore he is not believed except specifically when in his hand or the first time; but when they contradict him, he is never believed according to all; and likewise Ran in Gittin there briefly; and Rashba wrote: and you may ask whence for Abaye who says and teaches, etc. — perhaps because silence is like admission as written in Yevamot there; one may say this is what he means: the reason, etc., specifically not "I do not know" (believed), for otherwise it should teach "I do not know"; and what is written in Yevamot there "and whence that he is believed," etc., refers to what is written above "whence for us from Scripture," etc., and still "whence for us from Scripture"; and what is written "know that it teaches," etc. — the discussion there follows that reasoning they said in Keritot 12a: the reason of the rabbis is because a person is believed, etc.; but Abaye holds the reason is because of migo — we resolve his words; and for that language at the beginning, because he is believed — when the rabbis reject because they are not believed when contradicted, it is because of migo. And what it says "and it is necessary," etc. — this is what he means: one might have thought the reason is not credibility but because silence is like admission — see there where he elaborated, and Ran brought them; but he wrote that Tosafot's view is primary, as those discussions prove; except the reason silence is like admission is because of the witness's testimony, for it is a decree of Scripture that whoever is silent, the witness is believed; therefore whoever the witness is not believed — meaning a robber and the like — he is not believed. And with this what he challenged — why does it say "he is believed," and likewise what he challenged from what is written "I am not a robber," etc. — is resolved; and these are Rava's words: there is no matter of sexual impropriety, etc., meaning in sexual impropriety one witness is not believed at all and he is like a robber or disqualified; and what is written in Yevamot there "and whence because," etc. — this is what he means: whence is he believed even when saying "I know," for perhaps he does not know like his contradiction; but specifically where he was silent; and the case of King Yannai — perhaps he was silent at first — and likewise certainly within twenty-four hours — see there:
And if not, etc. As written in Ketubot 22a and in Even HaEzer siman 152 seif 6:
And whoever is believed, etc. As written: we counted him in place of witnesses — we do not say in chapter 6 of Bava Metzia (chapter 1 2) and chapter 3 of Bava Batra; and learn from this:
Nevertheless for him, etc. As written in Ketubot 23b; and in Tosafot Yevamot 47a s.v. he is believed, etc., and s.v. and there is not, etc.:
The massacre of qua. A.S.:
And all disqualified for testimony, etc. But Ran wrote they are not believed — for this is what he means: if you believe me that he is not a robber, etc., as above — requires investigation; and likewise what he wrote "unless he is suspected," etc. — behold we say above siman 119 seif 7 "and regarding another's," etc., for we establish in chapter 8 of Yoma and in Bekhorot 35b like R. Shimon ben Gamliel, who said one is believed regarding his fellow's, etc.; except to permit he is believed even the suspected; but to forbid, he is believed by force of his testimony — all the disqualified are not believed, as above; and likewise Shach challenged — requires investigation: (Collection) And all disqualified for testimony, etc. For we establish: one suspected of one matter is not suspected, etc. [and in Tosafot Bekhorot 36a s.v. say, etc.] as written in siman 119 seif 4 and seif 7: If not, etc. See there seif 7, that it is not as he wrote "and regarding another's," etc.; but according to the Rav's words, that is primary, as he wrote (in s.k. 18) (end of quote):

pitchei_teshuva.he: נאמן. עבה"ט מ"ש ועפ"ז כו' אפילו הוא בידו כיון דלית ליה מגו. ועי' בדגמ"ר שכתב אם כונתו שגם קודם הבישול היה בידו אך עתה לא מקרי בידו שכבר נתבשל א"כ מיירי דלא א"ל כן בפעם ראשון אבל אין דין זה מוכרח שכיון שלא הוציאו מת"י עדיין וא"א לבא לידי מכשול לא נחוץ להגיד לו בפעם ראשון ולכן נראה דכוונתו שקודם הבישול לא היה בידו כלל רק עתה מסרו לידו אחר הבישול עכ"ד ובזה מתורץ הקושיא שהביא הבה"ט של מהרי"ט ז"ל בשם אא"ז הגאון מהר"ם א"ש ז"ל ע"ש ודו"ק:
pitchei_teshuva.en: Believed. Avodat HaTaharah wrote, and accordingly, etc. — even if it is in his hand, since he has no migo. And see in Darkei Moshe who wrote: if his intent is that even before cooking it was in his hand but now it is not called "in his hand" since it was already cooked — then it deals that he did not tell him so the first time; but this law is not necessary, for since he did not take it out from tithe status yet and it is impossible to come to a stumbling block, he need not tell him the first time; therefore it appears his intent is that before cooking it was not in his hand at all, only now they gave it into his hand after cooking — end of his words; and with this the difficulty that Avodat HaTaharah brought from Mahariyat in the name of R. Azriel Gaon Maharam Ash is resolved — investigate.

yad_avraham.he: (סימן קכ"ז סעיף א') והוא שיאמר לו נתנסך יינן בפניך או שא"ל ידעת כו'. ועיין בש"ך שפי' דאי לאו הכי לא הוי שתיקה כהודאה דהא דשותק מפני שאינו יודע בירור הדבר. וכן מפרש דברי הרמב"ם בפ"ט מהלכות נזירות שפסק אם שתק או נסתפק לו ה"ז מביא קרבן אפילו ע"פ ע"א. היינו שנסתפק לו ושותק מחמת כן ותרי גווני שתיקה קתני או מחמת הודאה או מחמת ספק שא"י הדבר ברור ואפ"ה העד נאמן. וגם הלח"מ בפ"ח דשגגות פי' כן דעת רבינו דבאינו יודע מביא קרבן. דהיינו ששותק מחמת שאינו ברור לו ולא באומר בפירוש אינו יודע אך בתשובת ש"י סי' מ"ג פי' כוונת הרמב"ם דאיירי שהעד אמר לו אתה ידעת שנולד לך ספק והוא שותק ולכך הוי כהודאה אבל בלא"ה לא הוי כהודאה ולכאורה נראה כוונת הרמב"ם דלא כהש"ך והלח"מ שפסק בספי"ב מהלכות מעשר המוכר פירות לחבירו ואחר שיצא מת"י אמר ללוקח טבל הן שורת הדין דאינו נאמן ומשמע דאינו מחויב להאמינו כשאינו יודע. וצ"ל דהיינו שמלמדין אותו שיאמר בפירוש שאינו מאמינו כמ"ש בהג"ה שם דאל"כ אלא שישתוק מחמת שאינו יודע נאמן העד לאסור. וכן צ"ל בכוונת הרמב"ם פ"ד מהל' ק"פ: שנולד לך ספק והוא שותק ולכך הוי כהודאה אבל בלא"ה לא הוי כהודאה ולכאורה נראה כוונת הרמב"ם דלא כהש"ך והלח"מ שפסק בספי"ב מהל' מעשר המוכר פירות לחבירו ואחר שיצא מת"י אמר ללוקח טבל הן שורת הדין דאינו נאמן ומשמע דאינו מחוייב להאמינו כשאינו יודע וצ"ל דהיינו שמלמדין אותו שיאמר בפירוש שאינו מאמינו כמ"ש בהג"ה שם דאל"כ אלא שישתוק מתמת שאינו יודע נאמן העד לאסור וכן צ"ל בכוונת הרמב"ם פ"ד מהל' ק"פ:
yad_avraham.en: (Siman 127 seif 1) And he must tell him "your wine was libated in your presence," or that he told him "you knew," etc. And see in Shach who explained that otherwise it is not silence like admission, for he is silent because he does not know the matter clearly. And likewise he explains the words of Rambam in chapter 9 of Laws of Nazirites, who ruled: if he was silent or was in doubt, he brings an offering even on the testimony of one witness — meaning he was in doubt and is silent on that account; and two types of silence are taught: either due to admission or due to doubt that the matter is not clear, and nevertheless the witness is believed. And likewise Lechem Mishneh in chapter 8 of Shegagot explained Rambam's view thus: regarding "he does not know," he brings an offering — meaning he is silent because it is not clear to him and he did not say explicitly "I do not know"; but in responsum Shav Yitzchak siman 43 he explained Rambam's intent that it deals when the witness told him "you knew that a doubt was born to you" and he is silent, and therefore it is like admission; but otherwise it is not like admission; and apparently Rambam's intent is not like Shach and Lechem Mishneh, who ruled in chapter 2 of Laws of Maaser that one who sells produce to his fellow and after it left from tithe status told the buyer "they are untithed" — the law is he is not believed; and it implies he is not obligated to believe him when he does not know; and it must be that we teach him to say explicitly that he does not believe him, as written in the gloss there — for otherwise if he is merely silent because he does not know, the witness is believed to forbid; and likewise must be Rambam's intent in chapter 4 of Laws of Terumot:

yad_ephraim.he: אם הוא בידו נאמן. עבה"ט ושו"ת ח"צ סי' ע"ט ליישב דברי הש"ך סימן קכ"ז שכתב דהב"י ס"ל דפועל נאמנותו משום מיגו ונ"מ לענין מפקיד יין מבושל לחבירו ואומר שנתנסך קודם שבא לידו דאי טעמא משום מיגו לא מהימן דביין מבושל לא היה לו מיגו מעולם ע"ש ועיין בספר בית אפרים על טריפות בקונ' הראיות שהארכתי בדברי הפמ"א והח"צ בזה:
yad_ephraim.en: If it is in his hand, he is believed. Avodat HaTaharah and responsum part 2 siman 79 — to settle Shach's words in siman 127, who wrote that Beit Yosef holds that a worker's credibility is because of migo; and there is a practical difference regarding one who deposits cooked wine with his fellow and says it was libated before it came into his hand — for if the reason is migo, he is not believed, for with cooked wine he never had migo — see there; and see in Beit Efrayim on treifot in Kuntras HaRe'ayot, where I elaborated on the words of Peri Megadim and part 2 on this:

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (סימן קכ"ז ש"ך ס"ק כ') כשר לדבר אחר שלא הוא. וקשה לי הא ממ"ש הרשב"א שם ראיה דמומר נאמן בשל אחרים דכמו דמומר אוכל נבילות נותנים לו סכין בדוק לשחוט. וכן בלוקח מן המקוליס שמוכרין שם נבילות ושחיטות דנאמן לומר שלקח מהכשר. ואפי' מן הסתם בלא אמירתו משום לא שביק היתירא וכ"ש במה שאינו בידו שנאמן לומר בשל מותר דכל שאין בו טורח כבדיקת סכין מותר עכ"ל והא מזה ראיה נשמע דגם במומר לאותו דבר נאמן בשל אחרים דהא במומר אוכל נבילות הוי מומר לאותו דבר וצע"ג:
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en:
It is written that he is not. It is hard for me to see Hashem’s promise of a faithful demon because of others as a bamboo, food is limited to give him a test knife to the diaspora. As well as a barrier from the melodies that sell a limited name, and that an artist’s teeth say he took from the talent. Indeed, without his utterance, it is not that Bika has been shot in what is not in his hand that he is trained to say because of the possibility that he does not bother as a test of a possible knife, and that in this regard, a model is heard in a gambler for the same faithful thing because of others Dea in the M
And Mary eats the same thing and says:
